Statement 1.2 (PDDL correspondence): a plan of the PDDL domain under ε-separation gives an event-ordered plan of §1.2 with the same cost and no larger makespan, and an event-ordered plan of makespan M gives PDDL plans of total-time at most M + Kε, so the PDDL front tends to the front of event-ordered plans as ε → 0.

Section 5 (greedy counterexamples): the per-PPP greedy of both papers, longest flights first to the least-loaded plane, misses front points: for d = (6, 10), c = (40, 20), t = 5, p = 2 it flies the landings of the front point (260, 60) in makespan 68, and for d = (1, 3), c = (9, 5), t = 4, p = 2 it misses (42, 12).
End of section 6.2: under (A1-NS), on instances with a city with d_x = d̄_x = 0, plans that are not event-ordered never beat the front of Corollary 6.10.
Conjecture 10.2: on the linear family of Theorem 10.1, the papers' per-PPP greedy reaches the front.
Conjecture 4.10: Theorem 4.7 holds under (S) and (AΔ), without (A1); equivalently, every feasible plan is weakly dominated in (cost, makespan) by a simple feasible plan.
Conjecture 6.7 (extended Proposition I): under (AΔ), the front equals the front of role configurations extended with shuttle triples, each adding exactly one landing, with exact makespans.
Corollary 2.7: if |X| = s, every link forest has at most t − p edges, and each of its trees has at most q_max = min(p, t − p + 1) planes.

Corollary 4.8: under (S) and (A1), the front is Min {(c(X), M(X)) : |X| = s, M(X) < ∞}, with M(X) the least max_k ℓ(X_k) over admissible partitions of X, and every front point is attained by a plan with exactly s central landings. Lean form: the minimal points of the plans equal those of the multiset points (multisetPoints), with an explicit p ≤ t; the attainment is Theorem 4.1 and is not restated.

Corollary 6.10 (non-symmetric front): under (A1-NS), F = Min A_eo = Min K, with K the points (c(cfg), m(cfg)) of role configurations on the p planes with passenger count t and least makespan m(cfg), and A_eo the points of event-ordered feasible plans.

Corollary 6.4 (one pick-up never waits harmfully) [W1]: under (AΔ-path), if every plane has at most one pick-up, or every plane at most one drop-off, then M_tmpl = max_k λ_k for every order and matching.
Corollary 8.3: E(T), and under (S) and (A1) the front, are computable in pseudo-polynomial time, so computing the front is not strongly NP-hard unless P = NP.

Definition 2.2 (admissible partition): a partition X_1..X_p is admissible if it has a parity matrix h ∈ {0,1}^{p×n} with h_{k,i} = 1 only where X_k(i) ≥ 1, every row sum ≡ |X_k| + 1 and every column sum even (mod 2). Lean form: Admissible X := ∃ h, IsParityWitness X h, with h k a set of cities of X_k (the ones of row k).

Definition 4.2 (role configuration): drop-offs Dr_k, pick-ups Pk_k and crossings Cr_k per plane, multisets of central cities with |Cr_k| odd and Σ_k Dr_k = Σ_k Pk_k city by city, with its passenger count, cost and role loads λ_k. Lean form: RoleConfig holds the three families, the parity and the balance; the groups and the role loads are separate definitions (RoleConfig.groups, RoleConfig.roleLoad), and the passenger count t appears as 2t − p landings.

Lemma 1.1 (dominating subset): if S' ⊆ S ⊆ K² with S' finite and every point of S weakly dominated by a point of S', then Min S = Min S', and every point of S is weakly dominated by a point of Min S. Lean form: Min S = Min S' in any partial order, without finiteness; the second clause, domination by a point of Min S, is not part of the Lean statement.

Lemma 2.1: on every route from C_I to C_G, the number of segments of type A (C_I to C_G) exceeds the number of type Ā (C_G to C_I) by one. Lean form: counts the landing records of a feasible plane by the hub they are entered from and left towards (#A = #Ā + 1), the reading of Step 1 of Theorem 4.7 in which a central leg passes through C_G; VChain.countP_isA is the same count on visits.
Lemma 2.3 (integer form) [A′]: a partition is admissible iff some h̃ ∈ ℕ^{p×n} has h̃_{k,i} ≤ X_k(i), Σ_i h̃_{k,i} ≡ |X_k| + 1 for every plane k and Σ_k h̃_{k,i} ≡ 0 for every city i (mod 2).

Lemma 2.4 (component form): (a) a partition is admissible iff every connected component of the plane-city graph H (k joined to i when X_k(i) ≥ 1) has an even number of even planes; (b) then every spanning forest of H contains the support of some parity matrix.
Lemma 2.5: for every parity matrix and every plane k, h_k ≤ |X_k| − 1.

Lemma 2.6 (link forest) [LF]: a partition is admissible iff it has a link forest, and an admissible partition has one with at most one edge of each label at each plane. Lean form: link forests are lists of rooted link trees satisfying (F2), whose groups equal the X_k as a multiset; the second clause (at most one edge of each label at each plane) is not formalised.

Lemma 2.8 (few touched cities) [B′]: for an admissible partition with |X| = s, (a) every parity matrix touches at most t − p cities, (b) one with the fewest entries 1 has an acyclic support and touches at most p − 1 cities, and (c) so some parity matrix touches at most min(p − 1, t − p) cities. Lean form: (c), (a) and the bound of (b) are the three declarations; the acyclic support of (b) appears as the linear independence of the edge vectors over ZMod 2 (IsParityWitness.exists_edgeCount_lt).

Lemma 2.9 (shared city): non-empty groups with Σ_k |X_k| ≡ p (mod 2) form an admissible partition if some city belongs to every even group, in particular if all groups share a city or all even groups are equal.

Lemma 3.1 (cleaning): every plan can be changed, keeping all routes (so cost, makespan and flight times), so that every journey is clean: its first flight is its only departure from C_I and its last flight its only arrival in C_G.

Lemma 3.2 (counting): a feasible plan has at least s = 2t − p segments, hence at least s landings in central cities. Lean form: 2t ≤ Σ_k (hub arrivals of plane k) + p, by counting legs, for any central flights; segments are counted as hub arrivals, and the consequence on landings is not stated separately.

Lemma 3.3 (segment durations): a segment visiting x_1..x_m lasts (a) at least d_{x_1} + d_{x_m} under (S); (b) under (AΔ), at least d_{x_j} + d̄_{x_j} for types A and Ā, 2d_{x_j} for B and 2d̄_{x_j} for B̄; and (c) exactly d_x + d̄_x, 2d_x or 2d̄_x if it is simple.

Lemma 3.4 (relaxation) [R]: under (S), every feasible plan with cost C and makespan M has non-empty multisets Y_1..Y_p with Σ_k |Y_k| = s, c(Y) ≤ C and ℓ(Y_k) ≤ F_k ≤ M, hence C ≥ L(⌊M/2⌋) with integer durations; no assumption on central flights is needed. Lean form: integer data, (S) as d̄ = d, an explicit p ≤ t, and 2δ(Y_k) ≤ M in place of ℓ(Y_k) ≤ F_k; relaxCost_oneplane_le_totalCost is the bound by L.

Lemma 4.3 (direct selection) [DS]: (a) in a simple plan with clean journeys every journey is C_I → x → C_G; (b) such a plan on planes Q, routes ending in C_G, gives a role configuration on Q with passenger count at least t, cost at most the plan's, λ_k ≤ F_k and groups inside the planes' landings.

Lemma 4.4 (shrinking) [SH]: a role configuration on Q with t(cfg) > t ≥ |Q| shrinks, by deleting landings, to one with passenger count exactly t whose cost, role loads and groups are no larger. Lean form: stated by landing count (s + 2N landings down to s ≥ p) with every role multiset shrinking, so cost, role loads and groups do not grow; Admissible.exists_shrink is the partition form used by Theorem 4.7.

Lemma 4.5 (parity) [PAR]: for a role configuration on Q with passenger count t, the groups X_k = Dr_k + Pk_k + Cr_k form an admissible partition of a multiset of size 2t − |Q|, with the same cost. Lean form: admissibility of the groups, with the witness h_{k,i} = (Dr_k(i) + Pk_k(i)) mod 2 (RoleConfig.isParityWitness_witness); size and cost hold by definition.

Lemma 4.6 (adding a plane) [AP]: an admissible partition of q planes with 2t − q landings and t ≥ q + 1 gives an admissible partition of q + 1 planes with 2t − q − 1 landings, no larger cost and no larger max_k δ(Y_k).

Lemma 6.2 (relaxed role loads): under (AΔ), every feasible plan with cost C and makespan M gives drop-off, pick-up and crossing multisets with |Cr_k| odd, balanced in total only, passenger count t, cost at most C and λ_k ≤ F_k ≤ M, so L_NS(T) bounds every plan of makespan at most T, shuttle triples included.

Lemma 6.3 (template) [N3]: the template of a role configuration with orders and a link matching is a schedule of makespan M_tmpl = max(max_k λ_k, max over links of Pre + d_i + d̄_i + Suf), and every schedule of the same configuration, orders and matching takes at least M_tmpl; no assumption on durations is needed.

Lemma 6.8 (event order): (a) a plan is event-ordered iff its next-leg relation has no cycle; (b) in a simple plan with clean journeys, a cycle passes through a central city with d_x = d̄_x = 0; (c) templates of role configurations and the plans of Theorem 4.1 are event-ordered.

Lemma 7.2: the one-plane table satisfies G[m][τ] = min{c(Y) : |Y| = m, δ(Y) ≤ τ} (∞ if there is none), and G is non-increasing in τ. Lean form: the least cost when an m-multiset with δ ≤ τ exists, with oneplane_eq_top_iff for the ∞ case; the monotonicity in τ is not stated.
Lemma 7.7 (Pareto sets): for a binary operation ⊗ on K² monotone in the product order and finite A, B, Min(A ⊗ B) = Min(Min A ⊗ Min B) and Min(A ∪ B) = Min(Min A ∪ Min B).

Lemma 9.2 (potentials) [X2]: in a finite graph, a map V to K ∪ {∞} with V(target) ≤ 0 and V(u) ≤ wt(u, v) + V(v) on every arc gives V(source) at most the weight of every path from the source to the target.

Lemma 9.3 (default potentials): the potentials V_0 built from the one-plane table (L_rest when σ = ∅, max over a ∈ σ of L^a otherwise) satisfy V_0(target) = 0 and V_0(u) ≤ wt(u, v) + V_0(v) on every arc of the σ-graph.

Claim of EvoCOP 2015 (Algorithm 1) and arXiv:2304.14659 (§3.2): for a fixed multiset of landings (a PPP), the greedy that gives the longest flights first to the least-loaded plane schedules it optimally, so the fronts ZenoSolver computes are the true Pareto fronts.

Assumption of arXiv:2304.14659, Conjecture 6.5 of the note: under (AΔ-path), every role configuration has orders and a link matching whose template has makespan max_k λ_k, and in its front-level form the front is the Pareto set of (cost, max_k λ_k) over role configurations.

Proposition 6.5 (harmful waiting): for n = 2, d = (3, 19), d̄ = (3, 11), c = (5, 1), t = 7, p = 4 and no central flights, (A1-NS) and (AΔ-path) hold, the cheapest role configuration with every λ_k ≤ 73 costs 14, and no plan of makespan at most 73 costs less than 18.

Proposition 6.6 (imbalance-vector DP) [N5]: the DP over planes with states (k, j, v), v the imbalance vector restricted to ‖v‖₁ ≤ t − p, has shortest path from (0, 0, 0) to (p, s, 0) of weight E_NS(T), the least cost of a role configuration with role loads at most T.

Proposition 7.1: under (S) and (A1), F = {(E(T), 2T) : T ∈ ℕ, E(T) < E(T − 1)}, with E(−1) = ∞ and makespans in units of g. Lean form: (C, 2T) is a minimal admissible point iff E(T) = C and E(T') > C for every T' < T, joined to the plans' front by Corollary 4.8 (minimal_achievable_iff_admissiblePoints); makespans are not rescaled by g.

Proposition 7.10 (ends of the front) [END]: under (S), with κ = ⌈s/p⌉, every plan has makespan at least 2 d_min κ and costs at least s c_min, both attained; (s c_min, 2 d_cheap κ) is the cheapest front point; and with integer durations E(T) < ∞ iff T ≥ d_min κ and E(T) = s c_min iff T ≥ d_cheap κ, and likewise for L.
Proposition 7.3: L(T) ≤ E(T) ≤ U_3(T) ≤ U(T), with L the relaxation and U_3, U the cheapest link forests of trees of at most three and two planes.
Proposition 7.4: if q_max ≤ 2 (p ≤ 2 or t ≤ p + 1) then E = U, and if q_max ≤ 3 (p ≤ 3 or t ≤ p + 2) then E = U_3.

Proposition 7.8 (Pareto-set variant) [PS]: with the σ-graph's arc weights replaced by finite Pareto sets of (cost, load) options combined by (c + c', max(τ, τ')), the set at (p, s, ∅) is the Pareto set of (c(X), max_k δ(X_k)) over admissible partitions with |X| = s and loads at most T_hi, the front points under (S) and (A1).
Proposition 7.9 (dominance) [DOM]: if d_{i'} ≤ d_i and c_{i'} ≤ c_i for cities i ≠ i', removing city i leaves E(T) and L(T) unchanged at every T, and under (S) and (A1) the front unchanged.

Proposition 8.2 (fixed p): for p = 2 deciding M(X) ≤ 2T stays NP-complete, even with positive durations, and for every fixed p it is solvable in time polynomial in n, s and T, so it is weakly NP-complete.
the per-PPP greedy of both papers is not optimal

Theorem 10.1 (linear family): under (S), with d_i = i and c_i = α − βi (β ≥ 0, α ≥ βn), L(T) = E(T) = αs − βΦ(T) for every T ≥ κ and ∞ below, with Φ(T) = (p − ρ) min(T, n q_0) + ρ min(T, n (q_0 + 1)), so the front is in closed form whatever the central flights.

Theorem 4.1 (achievability): under (S), every admissible partition X_1..X_p of a multiset X with |X| = s is flown by a feasible plan whose central landings are exactly X (cost c(X)) and whose makespan is max_k ℓ(X_k), using no central flight. Lean form: an explicit p ≤ t; the landings equal X up to relabelling the planes; that plane k flies for ℓ(X_k) and picks up at most one passenger holds for the construction (LTree.routes) but is not in the statement.

Theorem 4.7 (converse): under (S) and (A1), every feasible plan with cost C, makespan M and flight times F_k is dominated by an admissible partition X_1..X_p of a multiset X with |X| = s, c(X) ≤ C and ℓ(X_k) ≤ F_k ≤ M. Lean form: integer data, (S) as d̄ = d, (A1) as Network.A1, an explicit p ≤ t, and 2δ(X_k) ≤ M in place of ℓ(X_k) ≤ F_k.
Theorem 4.9 (bridge) [B3]: under (S) and (A1), the front of the variant in which planes may end anywhere and the makespan is the last arrival equals the front F. Lean form: an explicit p ≤ t.

Theorem 6.1 (converse to role configurations) [N1]: under (A1-NS), every feasible plan with cost C and makespan M gives a role configuration on all p planes with passenger count t, cost at most C and λ_k ≤ F_k ≤ M; (AΔ) is not needed. Lean form: an explicit p ≤ t, the passenger count as 2t − p landings, and λ_k ≤ M in place of λ_k ≤ F_k.

Theorem 6.9 (schedulable domination) [SD]: under (A1-NS), every feasible plan with cost C and makespan M is dominated by a role configuration on all p planes with passenger count t and cost at most C, with orders and a link matching whose template has makespan at most M; no event order, (AΔ) or (AΔ-path) is needed. Lean form: an explicit p ≤ t, the note's standing assumption (not_schedulableDomination: it fails for t < p); the configuration is a valid scheduled configuration with 2t − p landings, and the bound is on its closed form Sched.tmpl, the formula of Lemma 6.3, not on a template schedule.

Theorem 7.5 (link-forest DP): For[p][s] = E(T), and given G the DP takes O(n q_max² s² T + p q_max s²) time and O(q_max s T + n q_max s + p s) memory per level. Lean form: the memoised DP (treeBoundAt) equals E(T) for 1 ≤ p and T ≤ Tmax; the complexity is not formalised.
Theorem 7.6 (σ-DP) [Claim C]: the shortest path from (0, 0, ∅) to (p, s, ∅) in the σ-graph has weight E(T). Lean form: the memoised σ-DP (sigmaBoundAt) equals E(T) for 1 ≤ p ≤ t and T ≤ Tmax.
Theorem 8.1: deciding M(X) ≤ 2T, with d, X, p and T as input, is strongly NP-complete.

Theorem 9.1 (end to end) [X3]: if a certificate's four obligations hold (a simulated plan for every point, no plan faster than the first, a lower bound on every gap, no plan cheaper than the last), its points are exactly the front F. Lean form: Cert.check = true implies IsParetoFront for every table of central flights satisfying (A1), or for every table if all gaps are relaxed; the obligations are the checker's tests.
